newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq surges after weak CPI, paced by tech group.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq surges after weak CPI, paced by tech group.

text.p: Soothing inflation data and a renewed interest in the high techs propelled Nasdaq to its largest single-day point gain since early August and its seventh biggest ever.

The Nasdaq Composite Index, which is larded with technology stocks, was up 22.86 points, or 1.96 percent, at 118.67 at its unofficial close, its biggest one-day gain since it rallied 26.07 points on August 2.
Advancers led decliners by 2365 to 1709 on volume of about 643 million shares.

"The perception last month was that we are going into a period of high inflation. Suddenly, the perception is that we are not," said Brett Discher, vice-president in charge of equity trading at Dain Bosworth.

In addition to a lower than expected August consumer price index, which Discher said was the main driving force behind the rally, SoundView Financial said it raised its short-term weighting in technology to overweight from average.
Further impetus for the techs came via Merrill Lynch, which upgraded its rating on high tech giant IBM to near-term strong buy from accumulate.
